chapters.title: What changed - and can we trust it?
copy: Familiar anchor: a shared notebook with numbered history
State: the information a program currently holds
Frame Chains: linked, checkable records of changing software state
Why it matters: a convincing screen alone cannot establish an allowed change
chapters.narration: When a shared notebook changes, numbered history helps you see what happened without erasing earlier pages. Software needs something similar. State is the information a program currently holds. Frame Chains organizes that changing state as records that can be checked, linked, and replayed. A convincing screen is not enough: we need to know which change was allowed and which accepted state can still be trusted.

chapters.title: A frame is a data record
copy: Frame: one data record, not a movie picture
Chain: an ordered history linked to earlier records
Hash: a data fingerprint, not proof that a story is true
Accepted head: latest record that passed
chapters.narration: A frame is one recorded event or state description, not a picture in a movie. A chain links those records into a checkable history. A hash is a fingerprint computed from data: it can reveal changed bytes, but cannot by itself prove a story or a cause. A verifier checks the recorded data and rules. The accepted head is the latest record that passed those checks.

chapters.title: Watch the rule, not just the world
copy: Proof models: fictional programs testing specific rules
Branch: a separate continuation of history
Projection: another view of the same history
Live replay: a running app you can pause and operate
chapters.narration: These ten worlds are proof models: deliberately simplified programs that test specific rules, not real colonies or conscious digital people. A branch is a separate continuation of history. A projection or lens is a different interface onto the same history. A live replay is a running application you can pause and operate. Watch a valid change succeed, a bad change get refused, and the accepted state remain intact.
